I can't rule out to (1,6,6) or to (2,6,7) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (1,6,6).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to (1,4,6), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4,7); going to (1,6,4) would wall in number 22, the last number; going to (2,6,7), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. Going to (4,4,7) would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes to (2,2,7).
Going to (4,2,7) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (2,1,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (1,2,6).
The line must go to (2,1,6): to (1,2,4) is number 20, which comes later.
I can't rule out to (4,1,6) or to (2,1,4) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (4,1,6).

Going to number 8, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (7,4,6). So the line goes to (7,2,6).
Number 8 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (4,2,7): to (6,4,7) is number 10, which comes later.
Going to (6,7,6) would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (6,4,7).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,4,6).
Cell (6,7,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,7,4).
Going to (7,6,4), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (6,7,2).
Going to (7,6,2) would leave both cell (7,6,4) and cell (6,6,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,6,1).
Going to (6,4,1), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (7,6,2).
Cell (7,6,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,2,4).
Going to (4,1,2) would force the line onto number 18 before its turn. So the line goes to (2,1,4).
Number 17 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (4,1,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,2,1).
Going to (1,4,2) would force the line onto number 21 before its turn. So the line goes to (1,2,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,4,4).
Cell (1,4,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,6,2).
